title: Twelve Emotions
subtitle: The Evolutionary Calculus and Neural Circuitry of Human Feeling
profile: B/C: Biological, Neural & Affective Control Loops + Decision Theory & Game-Theoretic Equilibria

chapters.title: The Dual-Road Alarm
chapters.subtitle: Joseph LeDoux's Thalamic Shortcut and Patient S.M.'s Bilateral Amygdala Calcification
chapters.historical_anchor: Joseph LeDoux's 1986–1996 auditory fear-conditioning pathway tracing in rats at Cornell and NYU (the 12-millisecond thalamo-amygdala low road versus the 24-millisecond thalamo-cortico-amygdala high road), paired with Justin Feinstein, Ralph Adolphs, and Antonio Damasio's 2011–2013 University of Iowa studies of Patient S.M. (Urbach-Wiethe ECM1 bilateral amygdala calcification) inhaling 35 percent carbon dioxide.
chapters.exit_fact: Within eight to fifteen seconds of inhaling a single breath of thirty-five percent carbon dioxide, Patient S.M. and two other bilateral amygdala-lesioned patients experienced full autonomic panic attacks and tore off their breathing masks—proving that internal suffocation alarms bypass the amygdala entirely via acid-sensing chemoreceptors in the brainstem.

chapters.title: The Pathogen Shield
chapters.subtitle: Paul Rozin's Fudge Trials and the Insular Cortex Hijack From Toxins to Taboos
chapters.historical_anchor: Paul Rozin, Linda Millman, Carol Nemeroff, and April Fallon's 1986–1987 University of Pennsylvania experiments on the laws of sympathetic magic (sterilized cockroach in juice and chocolate fudge shaped like dog feces), paired with Andrew Calder's 2000 insular lesion case and Hanah Chapman's 2009 facial electromyography of the levator labii muscle across bitter quinine, fecal photographs, and Ultimatum Game unfairness.
chapters.exit_fact: In Hanah Chapman's 2009 electromyography trials at the University of Toronto, receiving an unfair nine-to-one dollar split in an economic game triggered the exact same levator labii superioris upper-lip curl and anterior insula activation evolved to spit bitter plant alkaloids out of the mouth.

chapters.title: The Credible Threat
chapters.subtitle: Robert Frank's Commitment Problem and Why Irrational Retaliation Wins Rational Bargaining
chapters.historical_anchor: Thomas Schelling's 1960 strategic commitment paradox and Robert H. Frank's 1988 Passions Within Reason commitment model explaining why visible autonomic anger deters theft when prosecution costs exceed stolen value, validated by Alan Sanfey and Jonathan Cohen's 2003 Princeton fMRI Ultimatum Game trials.
chapters.exit_fact: In Alan Sanfey and Jonathan Cohen's 2003 Princeton fMRI trials, whenever a player's anterior insula response to an unfair eight-to-two dollar split exceeded activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, the angry player rejected the free two dollars so that the greedy proposer walked away with zero.

chapters.title: The Severed Attachment Loop
chapters.subtitle: Colin Murray Parkes's Widowhood Mortality Studies and Nucleus Accumbens Yearning
chapters.historical_anchor: John Bowlby and Colin Murray Parkes's 1969–1972 British Medical Journal bereavement studies tracking 4,486 widowers (finding a 40 percent mortality surge in the first six months), Hikaru Sato's 1990 Takotsubo catecholamine cardiomyopathy, and Mary-Frances O'Connor's 2008 UCLA fMRI study of prolonged grief.
chapters.exit_fact: In Mary-Frances O'Connor's 2008 UCLA neuroimaging trials, viewing a photograph of a deceased loved one activated the dorsal anterior cingulate pain network in all bereaved women, but only those with prolonged grief disorder simultaneously fired the nucleus accumbens—turning an unrewritable attachment bond into a persistent dopamine craving.

chapters.title: The Public Gaze Versus the Private Debt
chapters.subtitle: June Tangney's Prisoner Studies and the Fork Between Hiding and Repair
chapters.historical_anchor: Ruth Benedict's 1946 and Helen Block Lewis's 1971 shame-versus-guilt distinction, June Price Tangney and Jeff Stuewig's 2007–2014 longitudinal study of 476–550 Virginia county jail inmates tracking post-release criminal recidivism, and Daniel Sznycer's 2016–2018 cross-cultural welfare trade-off calibration studies.
chapters.exit_fact: Across Daniel Sznycer's 2016 and 2018 cross-cultural trials spanning fifteen societies from the United States and India to Ecuadorian horticulturalists, the intensity of shame people felt for twenty-nine specific failings correlated at 0.84 with the exact degree to which local neighbors devalued a community member for that same trait.

chapters.title: The Relative Payoff Trap
chapters.subtitle: Sarah Brosnan's Capuchin Cucumber Revolt and Ventral Striatum Social Comparison
chapters.historical_anchor: Sarah Brosnan and Frans de Waal's 2003 Emory University capuchin monkey (Cebus apella) cucumber-versus-grape token exchange experiment, Ernst Fehr and Klaus Schmidt's 1999 inequity-aversion utility equation, and Hidehiko Takahashi's 2009 fMRI pairing of anterior cingulate envy with ventral striatum Schadenfreude.
chapters.exit_fact: In Hidehiko Takahashi's 2009 functional magnetic resonance imaging trials in Chiba, Japan, the stronger a participant's dorsal anterior cingulate pain response had been while reading about a rival's triumph, the stronger their ventral striatum dopamine reward burst fired moments later when that same rival suffered a sudden misfortune.

chapters.title: The Information Gap
chapters.subtitle: George Loewenstein's Curiosity Curve and Dopamine Firing for Non-Instrumental Answers
chapters.historical_anchor: Daniel Berlyne's 1954 epistemic curiosity framework, George Loewenstein's 1994 Carnegie Mellon information-gap theory (inverted-U curiosity curve over partial knowledge), Ethan Bromberg-Martin and Okihide Hikosaka's 2009–2011 macaque midbrain dopamine and lateral habenula recordings for non-instrumental advance information, and Matthias Gruber's 2014 UC Davis hippocampal memory study.
chapters.exit_fact: In Matthias Gruber and Charan Ranganath's 2014 UC Davis neuroimaging trials, waiting fourteen seconds for the answer to a high-curiosity trivia question ramped up substantia nigra and nucleus accumbens dopamine activity so strongly that participants also remembered unrelated bystander faces flashed during the waiting period twenty-four hours later.

chapters.title: The Involuntary Blush
chapters.subtitle: Charles Darwin's Reddening Paradox and Dacher Keltner's Appeasement Signal
chapters.historical_anchor: Charles Darwin's 1872 analysis of blushing in The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals, Stefan Mellander's 1982 demonstration of unique beta-adrenergic sympathetic vasodilation in human facial veins, and Dacher Keltner and Matthew Feinberg's 1997–2012 UC Berkeley nonverbal appeasement and economic trust game experiments.
chapters.exit_fact: In Matthew Feinberg, Robb Willer, and Dacher Keltner's 2012 Berkeley economic experiments, participants handed fifty percent more real money in trust games to partners who blushed, looked down, and touched their faces after an awkward social mishap than to partners who remained composed.

chapters.title: The Play-Bow Breath
chapters.subtitle: Jaak Panksepp's Ultrasonic Rat Tickling and the Metabolic Cost of Social Grooming
chapters.historical_anchor: Jaak Panksepp and Jeffrey Burgdorf's 1997–2000 Bowling Green discovery of 50-kilohertz ultrasonic chirps in tickled juvenile rats, Robert Provine's 1996–2000 acoustic field study of 1,200 natural human conversations, and Robin Dunbar's 2012 Oxford endorphin pain-threshold and primate grooming-scale trials.
chapters.exit_fact: In Robin Dunbar's 2012 Oxford pain-tolerance trials, fifteen minutes of synchronized group laughter raised participants' ischemic blood-pressure-cuff pain thresholds by roughly ten percent while solitary viewing or polite conversation left thresholds flat—allowing choral laughter to broadcast an endogenous opioid bond to three times as many partners at once as fingertip grooming.

chapters.title: The Swiss Mercenary's Fever
chapters.subtitle: Johannes Hofer's Seventeenth-Century Medical Diagnosis and Sedikides's Thermoregulatory Buffer
chapters.historical_anchor: Johannes Hofer's June 1688 University of Basel medical dissertation coining nostalgia (nostos + algos) among Swiss mercenaries hearing the Alpine Kuhreihen melody, and Constantine Sedikides, Tim Wildschut, and Xinyue Zhou's 2006–2012 Southampton and Sun Yat-sen University experiments on social connectedness and cold-room thermoregulation.
chapters.exit_fact: In Xinyue Zhou, Tim Wildschut, and Constantine Sedikides's 2012 thermoregulation trials, volunteers placed in a chilly sixteen-degree-Celsius room spontaneously experienced higher nostalgia than peers in warm rooms, and recalling a nostalgic memory allowed participants to hold their hands submerged in four-degree-Celsius ice water for thirty-four seconds compared to twenty-seven seconds for controls.

chapters.title: The Asymmetric Curl
chapters.subtitle: Paul Ekman's Unilateral Lip Raise and John Gottman's Four-Horseman Divorce Predictor
chapters.historical_anchor: Paul Ekman and Wallace Friesen's 1986 cross-cultural identification of Action Unit 14 (unilateral buccinator and zygomaticus major contraction), and John Gottman and Robert Levenson's 1992–2002 University of Washington Love Lab longitudinal tracking of marital stability, the five-to-one affect balance equation, and partner infectious illness rates.
chapters.exit_fact: Across John Gottman and Robert Levenson's longitudinal University of Washington marriage studies, the exact count of unilateral Action Unit 14 contempt expressions flashed during a single fifteen-minute conflict conversation not only predicted divorce with over ninety percent accuracy, but also predicted how many infectious respiratory illnesses the targeted spouse suffered over the next four years.

chapters.title: The Upstream Reciprocity Engine
chapters.subtitle: Robert Trivers's Altruism Ledger and Sara Algoe's Find-Remind-and-Bind Amplification
chapters.historical_anchor: Robert Trivers's 1971 reciprocal altruism inequality, Monica Bartlett and David DeSteno's 2006 Northeastern University crashed-computer upstream reciprocity experiment, Martin Nowak and Sebastien Roch's 2007 mathematical theory of upstream reciprocity, and Sara Algoe's 2008–2012 UNC Chapel Hill find-remind-and-bind model.
chapters.exit_fact: In Monica Bartlett and David DeSteno's 2006 Northeastern University trials, participants whose crashed computers were rescued by a helpful confederate spent fifty percent more time completing tedious survey sheets for that benefactor and equally extended their helping time by fifty percent for a complete stranger they had never met.
